claims.text: Superconductivity in (TaNb)0.67(HfZrTi)0.33 is governed by local electron–phonon coupling.
Electron–phonon coupling is optimized when the alloy has a fully random atomic distribution.
Nanoscale atomic clustering disrupts the favorable electronic density of states.
Nanoscale atomic clustering disrupts phonon modes relevant to superconductivity.
Introducing nanoscale atomic clustering reduces the superconducting critical temperature.
The initial (TaNb)0.67(HfZrTi)0.33 material is a fully random solid solution.
The fully random state has high configurational entropy.
Prior DFT or KKR-CPA models have established lattice parameters for (TaNb)0.67(HfZrTi)0.33.
KKR-CPA is applicable to structural properties and short-range ordering in high-entropy alloys.
The degree of disorder versus short-range order alters local electron–phonon coupling.
The degree of disorder versus short-range order alters the density of states at the Fermi level.
A fully random configuration maximizes the favorable density of states at the Fermi level.
A fully random configuration creates an electron–phonon coupling environment that enhances Cooper pairing and superconductivity.
Atomic clustering introduces scattering centers.
Atomic clustering introduces local lattice distortions.
Scattering centers and local lattice distortions disrupt the uniform coupling required for robust superconductivity.
The fully disordered model will have a higher electron–phonon coupling constant than the clustered model.
The fully disordered model will have a higher density of states at the Fermi level than the clustered model.
The fully disordered model will have a higher predicted critical temperature than the clustered model.
The proposed mechanism is limited to HEA superconductors dominated by conventional electron–phonon pairing and may fail under strong electronic correlations or alternative pairing interactions.

contradictions.description: The conditions require identical electronic structure in the random and clustered models, while the mediator, mechanism, and predicted outcome require clustering to change the electronic density of states at the Fermi level.

The conditions state that local lattice distortions and interatomic distances will be controlled, whereas the mechanism identifies clustering-induced local lattice distortions as part of the causal pathway.
